subject: Accounting
title: IFAC and Global Ethics
description: A 60-second lesson on IFAC and Global Ethics.

hook.text: Accounting is global. So the International Federation of Accountants sets ethics for the whole world.

buildup.text: IFAC's International Ethics Standards Board publishes the IESBA Code used in over 130 countries.

discovery.text: The code covers integrity, objectivity, competence, confidentiality, and professional behavior.

twist.text: Enforcement varies widely—some countries rigorously enforce the code while others treat it as aspirational.

climax.text: A global standard aims to ensure that an accountant's ethics don't change at the border.

punchline.text: Ethics shouldn't depend on which country you're in.

quiz.question: What does the IESBA Code provide?
options: Global ethics standards for accountants in over 130 countries
Audit procedures for the Big Four only

details.summary: IFAC—the International Federation of Accountants—sets global ethical standards for the profession through the International Ethics Standards Board. This topic explains how global ethics codes are developed and adopted across different countries.
details.whyItMatters: In a globalized economy, inconsistent ethical standards create loopholes that bad actors exploit. IFAC works to establish a common ethical floor that all accountants worldwide should meet.
takeaways: IFAC represents over 180 member organizations across 135 countries
The IESBA Code of Ethics serves as the global baseline for accounting ethics
National professional bodies adopt IFAC standards or create equivalent local codes

faq.question: What is IFAC and what does it do for accounting ethics?
faq.answer: IFAC is the International Federation of Accountants, representing professional bodies in 135+ countries. Through its International Ethics Standards Board (IESBA), it develops the global Code of Ethics that establishes fundamental principles for all professional accountants.

faq.question: How are IFAC ethics standards adopted globally?
faq.answer: Member bodies in each country adopt the IESBA Code either directly or by developing national codes that meet or exceed IFAC standards. Some countries modify certain provisions to align with local laws while maintaining the core ethical principles.
